dedupe_keys.name: united states northeast distribution network analysis results

description: The US Northeast electric-network team publishes computed distribution-network metrics by census tract. The Harvard Dataverse result package includes node-level degree, betweenness, clustering, closeness and straightness indicators and tract-level summaries described in its own metadata. Coverage follows the northeastern circuits used in the study, not every United States feeder. Public access is free under CC BY 4.0. The metrics can help compare topology or prioritize structural-resilience scenarios, with model-pypsa offering a separate power-network modelling context. A caveat is that centrality measures describe a processed graph, not measured power flow, overload probability or outage consequence. Node definition, segmentation and tract clipping can change metric values substantially. The own repository description and ZIP manifest were read without downloading CSV files or recomputing graph measures. Cleaned geometries and original circuit layers are distinct companion deposits.
